_meta.purpose: Controlled fixture for the R4 feedback-loop experiment (eval_feedback.py). See docs/10 for the pre-registered protocol.
_meta.disclosure: These incidents are SYNTHETIC fixtures, not production data. They are derived from real chaos-run templates (OOM cured run 2026-07-06 and the rolled_back episodes 2026-07-04), with pods/namespaces anonymized. They exist to run a controlled A/B; they must be disclosed as synthetic in any slide or doc that cites results from them. The real `incidents` collection in the cluster is left untouched — the harness uses a disposable collection.
_meta.provenance: hand-authored 2026-07-08 by the eval design; mirrors the shape build_incident_document() writes (error_class + outcome + fix_applied + free text).

retrieval_seed.text: Incident KubePodOOMKilled on container app. Container was OOMKilled repeatedly; memory limit 32Mi exceeded under load. Fix applied: raised resources.limits.memory to 64Mi. Outcome: cured — pod healthy after the wait window, no further OOM.

Incident KubePodOOMKilled on container worker. Memory limit 128Mi exceeded. Fix applied: raised resources.limits.memory to 256Mi. Outcome: rolled_back — pod kept OOMing after the patch, remediation reverted. Root cause was a memory leak, not an undersized limit.

retrieval_seed.fix_applied: corrected missing env var via config
retrieval_seed.text: Incident KubePodCrashLoopBackOff on container api. Container exited non-zero on startup, crash loop. Fix applied: restored the missing DATABASE_URL env var. Outcome: cured — container started cleanly.
Incident KubePodCrashLoopBackOff on container scheduler. Repeated restarts after a config change. Fix applied: reverted to the previous config revision. Outcome: cured — restarts stopped.

Incident KubePodImagePullBackOff on container frontend. Image tag pointed to a non-existent registry tag. Fix applied: corrected the image tag to a published version. Outcome: cured — image pulled successfully.
Incident KubePodImagePullBackOff on container batch. Registry authentication failed, private image. Fix applied: attached the imagePullSecret to the service account. Outcome: cured.
Incident HighCPU on container api. Sustained CPU saturation against a 250m limit. Fix applied: raised resources.limits.cpu to 500m. Outcome: cured — CPU headroom restored.

Incident HighCPU on container ingest. CPU pegged at the 500m limit. Fix applied: raised resources.limits.cpu to 1000m. Outcome: rolled_back — a hot loop kept the CPU saturated regardless of the limit; remediation reverted, code fix required.

Incident HighMemory on container cache. Memory usage approaching the 256Mi limit under traffic. Fix applied: raised resources.limits.memory to 512Mi. Outcome: cured — usage stabilized below the new limit.
Incident HighMemory on container aggregator. Memory pressure near the 512Mi limit during batch windows. Fix applied: raised resources.limits.memory to 1Gi. Outcome: cured.

behavioral.note: 3-arm ablation. The ONLY variable that differs between the negative and positive arms is the outcome value (rolled_back vs cured), reflected identically in the incident text and metadata exactly as build_incident_document() writes it. This isolates the outcome LABEL as the causal variable.
behavioral.stimulus_rationale: A NEW OOM alert on a different pod/namespace than the seeded incident — tests generalization by error_class, not memorization of an exact string. oom-002 has a context-rich description (see docs/10), so the baseline model reliably proposes the memory bump; that gives the negative-knowledge signal headroom.

base_incident.text_template: Incident KubePodOOMKilled on container app in a prior deployment. Container was OOMKilled; memory limit 64Mi exceeded. Fix applied: raised resources.limits.memory to 128Mi (2x the previous limit). Outcome: {outcome}.

arms.name: control
arms.prediction: proposes the memory bump; confidence unmodified — no memory to consult

arms.name: negative
arms.prediction: SUPPRESSES the memory bump (or drops confidence / cites the prior failure), per DIAGNOSIS_PROMPT rule 'never propose a fix marked as failed'

arms.name: positive_ablation
arms.prediction: does NOT suppress the bump — same as control; isolates the label as causal
